cards.eli12: Security camera/history log for your AWS account.
cards.definition: Records API calls and account activity (who did what, when, from which IP address) across your AWS account for auditing, governance, compliance and security investigations. Event history shows the last 90 days by default; create a trail to store logs in S3 long term.
cards.official: AWS CloudTrail is a web service that records AWS API calls for your account and delivers log files to you. The recorded information includes the identity of the API caller, the time of the API call, the source IP address of the API caller, the request parameters, and the response elements that the AWS service returns.

cards.eli12: Use foundation models to build generative AI apps without making the model yourself.
cards.definition: Fully managed service for building generative AI applications with a choice of foundation models from Amazon and leading AI companies through a single API — customize them with your own data, with no infrastructure to manage.
cards.official: Amazon Bedrock is a fully managed service that makes foundational models (FMs) from Amazon and leading AI companies available through an API. With the Amazon Bedrock serverless experience, you can quickly get started, experiment with FMs, privately customize them with your own data, and seamlessly integrate and deploy FMs into your AWS applications.

cards.eli12: Put AWS compute close to a 5G network so apps respond super fast.
cards.definition: AWS infrastructure within telecom 5G networks for ultra-low-latency applications.
cards.official: Wavelength Zones provide you with the ability to build applications that deliver ultra-low latencies to 5G devices and end users. Wavelength deploys standard AWS compute and storage services to the edge of telecommunication carriers' 5G networks.

cards.hint: HOW is my AWS stuff doing?
cards.eli12: Dashboard and alarm system watching AWS resources.
cards.definition: Monitors performance of AWS resources and applications in real time using metrics, logs, dashboards and alarms. Alarms can trigger actions such as notifications (SNS) or Auto Scaling. Answers "how is it performing?" — not "who made this change?" (CloudTrail).
cards.official: Amazon CloudWatch is a web service that you can use to monitor and manage various metrics, and configure alarm actions based on data from those metrics.

cards.eli12: Protects against huge floods of bad traffic.
cards.definition: Managed DDoS protection. Shield Standard is automatic and free for all AWS customers (common network/transport-layer attacks). Shield Advanced is a paid tier with enhanced detection, 24/7 access to the Shield Response Team and DDoS cost protection.
cards.official: AWS Shield is a managed Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) protection service that safeguards web applications running on AWS. AWS Shield provides you with always-on detection and automatic inline mitigations that minimize application downtime and latency, so there is no need to engage Support to benefit from DDoS protection.

cards.eli12: Checks web requests and blocks bad ones.
cards.definition: Web application firewall that filters HTTP/HTTPS requests (Layer 7) with rules — block SQL injection, cross-site scripting, specific IP addresses or countries, and rate-limit requests. Deploys on CloudFront, Application Load Balancer, API Gateway and AppSync.
cards.official: AWS WAF is a web application firewall that helps protect your web applications or APIs against common web exploits and bots that may affect availability, compromise security, or consume excessive resources. AWS WAF gives you control over how traffic reaches your applications by enabling you to create security rules that control bot traffic and block common attack patterns, such as SQL injection or cross-site scripting.

cards.eli12: Put files/objects into buckets.
cards.definition: Scalable object storage for any amount of data, stored as objects in buckets. Buckets are created in a Region; names are globally unique (or unique per account and Region with the newer account regional namespace). Objects can be up to 50 TB. Designed for 99.999999999% (11 nines) durability. Also hosts static websites.
cards.official: Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) is an object storage service that offers industry-leading scalability, data availability, security, and performance. This means customers of all sizes and industries can use it to store and protect any amount of data for a range of use cases, such as websites, mobile applications, backup and restore, archive, enterprise applications, IoT devices, and big data analytics.

cards.eli12: A virtual computer/server you control.
cards.definition: Resizable virtual servers (instances) in the cloud — Infrastructure as a Service. You choose the instance type, AMI (OS image) and storage, and you manage the guest OS, patches and software. Billed per second (Linux) or per hour.
cards.official: Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) is a web service that provides secure, resizable compute capacity in the cloud. It is designed to make web-scale computing easier for developers.

cards.eli12: Give AWS code; AWS runs it without you managing servers.
cards.definition: Serverless compute that runs your code in response to events (S3 upload, API call, schedule) with no servers to manage. Scales automatically; you pay only for requests and compute time (per millisecond). Each invocation can run for up to 15 minutes.
cards.official: AWS Lambda lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers. You pay only for the compute time you consume—there is no charge when your code is not running.

cards.hint: WHO are you + WHAT can you do?
cards.eli12: Decides who can access what.
cards.definition: AWS Identity and Access Management controls who is authenticated and what they are authorized to do, using users, groups, roles and JSON policies. Global service, no extra charge. Access is denied by default; an explicit deny always overrides an allow.
cards.official: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) enables you to securely control access to AWS services and resources for your AWS users, groups, and roles. Using IAM, you can create and manage fine-grained access controls with permissions, specify who can access which services and resources, and under which conditions.

cards.eli12: AWS manages a traditional SQL database.
cards.definition: Managed relational (SQL) database service. Engines: Amazon Aurora, MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server and Db2. AWS automates hardware provisioning, patching, backups and recovery. Multi-AZ deployments add a standby in another AZ for high availability and automatic failover.
cards.official: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale a relational database in the cloud. It provides cost-efficient and resizable capacity while automating time-consuming administration tasks such as hardware provisioning, database setup, patching and backups.

cards.eli12: Fast database without a traditional relational design.
cards.definition: Fully managed, serverless NoSQL key-value and document database with single-digit-millisecond performance at any scale. Scales automatically; no servers to patch. Global tables provide multi-Region replication.
cards.official: Amazon DynamoDB is a key-value and document database that delivers single-digit millisecond performance at any scale. It's a fully managed, multi-Region database with built-in security, backup and restore, and in-memory caching for internet-scale applications.

cards.eli12: Analyze huge piles of business data.
cards.definition: Fully managed, petabyte-scale data warehouse that uses SQL to run complex analytic queries (OLAP/business intelligence) across large volumes of structured data. Columnar storage.
cards.official: Amazon Redshift is the most widely used cloud data warehouse. It makes it fast, simple and cost-effective to analyze all your data using standard SQL and your existing Business Intelligence (BI) tools.

cards.eli12: Get AWS compliance reports and agreements.
cards.definition: Self-service portal for on-demand, free access to AWS security and compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO certifications) — Artifact Reports — and to review and accept agreements such as the Business Associate Addendum (BAA) — Artifact Agreements.
cards.official: AWS Artifact is your go-to, central resource for compliance-related information that matters to you. It provides on-demand access to AWS security and compliance reports and select online agreements.

cards.eli12: Set a money limit and get alerts.
cards.definition: Set custom cost, usage, Reserved Instance or Savings Plans budgets and get alerts (email or SNS) when actual or forecasted spend crosses your threshold. Budget actions can automatically apply restrictions when a budget is exceeded.
cards.official: AWS Budgets gives you the ability to set custom budgets that alert you when your costs or usage exceed (or are forecasted to exceed) your budgeted amount.

cards.eli12: Look at AWS spending and usage patterns.
cards.definition: Visualize, understand and analyze your AWS costs and usage over time, filter and group by service, account or tag, forecast spend up to 12 months ahead, and get Reserved Instance and Savings Plans recommendations.
cards.official: AWS Cost Explorer has an easy-to-use interface that lets you visualize, understand, and manage your AWS costs and usage over time.

cards.eli12: Think of a parent account organizing and governing a family of AWS accounts.
cards.definition: Centrally manage and govern multiple AWS accounts: group accounts into organizational units (OUs), apply Service Control Policies (SCPs) that set the maximum permissions an account can use, and use consolidated billing for one bill and volume discounts.
cards.official: AWS Organizations helps you centrally manage and govern your environment as you grow and scale your AWS resources.

cards.hint: CAF = roadmap for moving the BUSINESS to cloud
cards.eli12: A guide that helps a company get its people, processes, and technology ready for cloud.
cards.definition: AWS guidance that helps organizations digitally transform and accelerate business outcomes through cloud adoption.
cards.official: The AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF) leverages AWS experience and best practices to help you digitally transform and accelerate your business outcomes through innovative use of AWS.

cards.eli12: First ask: How will cloud help our business win?
cards.definition: Demonstrates how cloud can accelerate business outcomes by identifying and prioritizing transformation opportunities.
cards.official: Envision phase focuses on demonstrating how cloud will help accelerate your business outcomes. It does so by identifying and prioritizing transformation opportunities across each of the four transformation domains in line with your strategic business objectives.

cards.hint: ALIGN = find the GAPS + get everyone aligned
cards.eli12: Figure out what skills/capabilities are missing and what is blocking teams.
cards.definition: Identifies capability gaps across the six CAF perspectives, cross-organizational dependencies, and stakeholder concerns.
cards.official: Align phase focuses on identifying capability gaps across the six AWS CAF perspectives, identifying cross-organizational dependencies, and surfacing stakeholder concerns and challenges. Doing so will help you create strategies for improving your cloud readiness, ensure stakeholder alignment, and facilitate relevant organizational change management activities.

cards.eli12: Put a small cloud initiative into production and prove it creates value.
cards.definition: Delivers pilot initiatives in production and demonstrates incremental business value.
cards.official: Launch phase focuses on delivering pilot initiatives in production and on demonstrating incremental business value. Pilots should be highly impactful and if/when successful they will help influence future direction.

cards.eli12: Take successful pilots and expand them so the whole business gets the benefit.
cards.definition: Expands production pilots and business value to desired scale and sustains cloud investment benefits.
cards.official: Scale phase focuses on expanding production pilots and business value to desired scale and ensuring that the business benefits associated with your cloud investments are realized and sustained.

cards.hint: CONFIG = WHAT did this RESOURCE look like/change to?
cards.eli12: Keeps a history of how your AWS resources are configured and checks whether they follow rules.
cards.definition: Assesses, audits, and evaluates AWS resource configurations; continuously records configuration changes and can evaluate them against desired configurations.
cards.official: AWS Config is a fully managed service that provides you with an AWS resource inventory, configuration history, and configuration change notifications to enable security and governance.
cards.notes: Config = resource-specific history. CloudTrail = account/API activity.

cards.hint: CATALOG = approved AWS stuff employees can choose
cards.eli12: Like a company-approved menu of IT products people are allowed to launch.
cards.definition: Lets organizations create and manage catalogs of approved IT services for use on AWS.
cards.official: AWS Service Catalog allows organizations to create and manage catalogs of IT services that are approved for use on AWS.

cards.eli12: Write a template describing what AWS resources you want; AWS builds them.
cards.definition: Infrastructure as code: describe AWS resources in a JSON or YAML template and CloudFormation provisions them as a stack — consistently and repeatably across accounts and Regions. No extra charge; pay for the resources created.
cards.official: AWS CloudFormation gives developers and systems administrators an easy way to create and manage a collection of related AWS resources, provisioning and updating them in an orderly and predictable fashion.

cards.eli12: Production workload and need around-the-clock technical help? Think Business.
cards.definition: For production workloads: 24/7 phone, email and chat access to Cloud Support Engineers, full set of Trusted Advisor checks, AWS Health API, and response in under 1 hour when a production system is down. Legacy plan: AWS is replacing it with the new plans, and current subscribers keep it through January 1, 2027.
cards.official: Business Support will be discontinued January 1, 2027. Customers with Business Support can continue using their existing plan or choose to upgrade to Business Support+ anytime before January 1, 2027.
cards.notes: Often the cost-effective answer when the requirement is production + 24/7 technical support.

cards.eli12: More help than Business for important workloads, but not the full Enterprise experience.
cards.definition: For production and business-critical workloads: everything in Business plus access to a pool of Technical Account Managers (TAMs), and response in under 30 minutes when a business-critical system is down. Legacy plan: AWS is replacing it with the new plans, and current subscribers keep it through January 1, 2027.
cards.official: On January 1, 2027, AWS will discontinue Enterprise On-Ramp. Throughout 2026, Enterprise On-Ramp customers will be automatically upgraded to AWS Enterprise Support during contract renewal or in periodic batches.

cards.eli12: Still building/testing? Think Developer, not 24/7 phone.
cards.definition: For testing and early development: business-hours email access to Cloud Support Associates, general architectural guidance; response under 24 business hours for general guidance and under 12 business hours for system impaired. No phone/chat, no 24/7. Legacy plan: AWS is replacing it with the new plans, and current subscribers keep it through January 1, 2027.
cards.official: Developer Support will be discontinued January 1, 2027. Customers with Developer Support can continue using their existing plan or choose to upgrade to Business Support+ anytime before January 1, 2027.
cards.notes: No 24/7 phone technical support.

cards.eli12: Big/critical AWS environment gets AWS experts plus a designated TAM.
cards.definition: For mission-critical workloads: a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), Concierge Support Team for billing and account help, Infrastructure Event Management, proactive guidance, and response in under 15 minutes when a business-critical system is down. AWS Security Incident Response is now included.
cards.notes: If the question says designated TAM, think Enterprise.

cards.hint: ELB = traffic COP directing cars into lanes
cards.eli12: Spreads incoming traffic across multiple healthy targets so one server doesn't get slammed.
cards.definition: Automatically distributes incoming traffic across multiple targets (EC2 instances, containers, IP addresses, Lambda) in one or more AZs and sends traffic only to healthy targets via health checks. Types: Application Load Balancer (HTTP/HTTPS, Layer 7), Network Load Balancer (TCP/UDP, Layer 4, ultra-low latency), Gateway Load Balancer.
cards.official: Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) automatically distributes incoming application traffic across multiple targets, such as Amazon EC2 instances, containers, and IP addresses. It can handle the varying load of your application traffic in a single Availability Zone or across multiple Availability Zones.
cards.notes: ELB distributes traffic; Auto Scaling changes capacity.

cards.eli12: Make copies of the database for people/apps that only need to read, taking pressure off the main database.
cards.definition: Read-only copies of an RDS database used to scale read-heavy workloads and, when supported, place reads closer to users.
cards.official: A read replica is a read-only copy of a DB instance. You can reduce the load on your primary DB instance by routing queries from your applications to the read replica.
cards.notes: Read Replica = performance/scaling. Multi-AZ = high availability/failover.

cards.hint: BEANSTALK = upload CODE, AWS handles the garden
cards.eli12: You give AWS your web app code; it handles much of the deployment and scaling while you can still access the resources.
cards.definition: Platform as a Service for deploying and scaling web applications: upload your code and it handles capacity provisioning, load balancing, auto scaling and health monitoring, while you keep full access to the underlying resources. No extra charge — you pay only for the resources it creates.
cards.official: AWS Elastic Beanstalk is an easy-to-use service for deploying and scaling web applications and services developed with Java, .NET, PHP, Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go, and Docker on familiar servers such as Apache, Nginx, Passenger, and Internet Information Services (IIS). You can simply upload your code, and AWS Elastic Beanstalk automatically handles the deployment, from capacity provisioning, load balancing, and auto scaling to application health monitoring.
cards.notes: No extra Beanstalk service charge; pay for underlying AWS resources.

cards.eli12: Dedicated private connection from your location to AWS.
cards.definition: Dedicated private network connection from your data center to AWS that doesn't travel over the public internet, giving more consistent performance, higher bandwidth and lower data-transfer costs. Not encrypted by default and takes weeks to set up.
cards.official: Direct Connect makes it easy to establish a dedicated network connection from your premises to AWS. Using Direct Connect, you can establish private connectivity between AWS and your data center, office, or co-location environment, which in many cases can reduce your network costs, increase bandwidth throughput, and provide a more consistent network experience than Internet-based connections.

cards.hint: LOCAL = AWS closer to your CITY
cards.eli12: Run AWS resources closer to users for low latency.
cards.definition: Extensions of an AWS Region placed in large metropolitan areas so latency-sensitive workloads (media rendering, real-time gaming, live video) run with single-digit-millisecond latency for nearby users.
cards.official: Local Zones provide you with the ability to place resources, such as compute and storage, in multiple locations closer to your end users.

cards.eli12: Cloud-built relational database compatible with MySQL/PostgreSQL.
cards.definition: AWS-built relational database compatible with MySQL (up to 5x faster than standard MySQL) and PostgreSQL (up to 3x faster). Keeps 6 copies of data across 3 AZs and backs up continuously to S3. Delivers commercial-database performance at a fraction of the cost.
cards.official: Amazon Aurora is a MySQL and PostgreSQL compatible relational database engine that combines the speed and availability of high-end commercial databases with the simplicity and cost-effectiveness of open source databases.

cards.eli12: Locations that deliver/cache content near users.
cards.definition: Sites in major cities worldwide — far more numerous than Regions — used by CloudFront (content caching), Route 53 (DNS) and Global Accelerator to serve users with lower latency.
cards.official: A data center that an AWS service uses to perform service-specific operations. For example, CloudFront uses edge locations to cache copies of your content, so the content is closer to your users and can be delivered faster regardless of their location. Route 53 uses edge locations to speed up the response to public DNS queries.

cards.eli12: Virtual firewall around resources such as EC2.
cards.definition: Virtual firewall at the instance (resource) level. Stateful — return traffic is automatically allowed. Supports allow rules only. By default all inbound traffic is denied and all outbound traffic is allowed.
cards.official: A security group controls the traffic that is allowed to reach and leave the resources that it is associated with. For example, after you associate a security group with an EC2 instance, it controls the inbound and outbound traffic for the instance. Security groups are stateful.

cards.eli12: Messages wait until a consumer is ready.
cards.definition: Fully managed message queue that decouples application components: producers send messages, consumers poll (pull) and process them at their own pace. Messages are kept up to 14 days. Standard queues (maximum throughput) and FIFO queues (exact order, exactly-once).
cards.official: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service that enables you to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. SQS eliminates the complexity and overhead associated with managing and operating message oriented middleware, and empowers developers to focus on differentiating work.

cards.eli12: Push one message to many subscribers.
cards.definition: Fully managed publish/subscribe service that pushes one message to many subscribers at once — email, SMS, mobile push, Lambda functions, SQS queues and HTTP endpoints.
cards.official: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) is a highly available, durable, secure, fully managed pub/sub messaging service that enables you to decouple microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. Amazon SNS provides topics for high-throughput, push-based, many-to-many messaging.

cards.eli12: AI analyzes images and video.
cards.definition: Machine learning image and video analysis service.
cards.official: Amazon Rekognition makes it easy to add image and video analysis to your applications using proven, highly scalable, deep learning technology that requires no ML expertise to use. With Amazon Rekognition, you can identify objects, people, text, scenes, and activities in images and videos, as well as detect any inappropriate content.

cards.eli12: AWS checks and gives optimization recommendations.
cards.definition: Inspects your AWS environment and recommends best-practice improvements across cost optimization, performance, security, fault tolerance, service limits (quotas) and operational excellence. Basic and Developer Support get core security and service-quota checks; Business Support and higher get the full set of checks.
cards.official: AWS Trusted Advisor is an online resource to help you reduce cost, increase performance, and improve security by optimizing your AWS environment.

cards.eli12: Checks workloads for known security weaknesses.
cards.definition: Automated vulnerability management: continuously scans EC2 instances, container images in ECR and Lambda functions for software vulnerabilities (CVEs) and unintended network exposure, and prioritizes findings.
cards.official: Amazon Inspector is a new automated vulnerability management service that continually scans AWS workloads for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure.

cards.eli12: Secure tunnel between your network/device and AWS.
cards.definition: Encrypted IPsec connection to AWS over the public internet. Quick and cheap to set up, but performance depends on the internet; often used as a backup to Direct Connect. Options: Site-to-Site VPN and Client VPN.
cards.official: AWS Virtual Private Network (Site-to-Site VPN) solutions establish secure connections between your on-premises networks, remote offices, client devices, and the AWS global network. Site-to-Site VPN is comprised of two services: AWS Site-to-Site VPN and AWS Client VPN.

cards.eli12: Your logically isolated network inside AWS.
cards.definition: Logically isolated virtual network for AWS resources.
cards.official: Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) lets you provision a logically isolated section of the AWS Cloud where you can launch AWS resources in a virtual network that you define. You have complete control over your virtual networking environment, including selection of your own IP address range, creation of subnets, and configuration of route tables and network gateways.

cards.eli12: Gateway that can give a VPC internet connectivity.
cards.definition: VPC component enabling communication between a VPC and the internet.
cards.official: Connects a network to the internet. You can route traffic for IP addresses outside your Amazon VPC to the internet gateway.

cards.eli12: Turns domain names into network addresses and routes users.
cards.definition: Highly available DNS service: domain registration, DNS routing and health checks. Routing policies include simple, weighted, latency-based, failover, geolocation and geoproximity.
cards.official: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service. It is designed to give developers and businesses an extremely reliable and cost-effective way to route users to internet applications by translating human-readable names, such as www.example.com, into the numeric IP addresses, such as 192.0.2.1, that computers use to connect to each other.

cards.eli12: Firewall at the subnet boundary.
cards.definition: Optional firewall at the subnet level. Stateless — return traffic must be explicitly allowed. Supports allow and deny rules, evaluated in number order. The default NACL allows all inbound and outbound traffic.
cards.official: When necessary, use network ACLs to provide stateless, coarse-grain network control. (AWS comparison: network ACLs operate at the subnet level, support allow and deny rules, and return traffic must be explicitly allowed.)

cards.eli12: A smaller IP-address section inside a VPC.
cards.definition: A range of IP addresses in a VPC, located in a single Availability Zone. A public subnet has a route to an internet gateway; a private subnet doesn't (it can reach the internet outbound through a NAT gateway).
cards.official: A subnet is a range of IP addresses in your VPC.

cards.eli12: Rules that tell network traffic where to go.
cards.definition: Routes that determine where network traffic is directed.
cards.official: A route table contains a set of rules, called routes, that are used to determine where network traffic from your VPC is directed.

cards.eli12: Lets private-subnet resources initiate outbound internet access.
cards.definition: Managed service placed in a public subnet that lets instances in private subnets start outbound connections to the internet (e.g., for software updates) while blocking connections initiated from the internet.
cards.official: You can use a network address translation (NAT) device. NAT maps multiple private IPv4 addresses to a single public IPv4 address.

cards.eli12: Delivers cached content from locations near users.
cards.definition: Content delivery network (CDN) that caches content (web pages, images, video, APIs) at edge locations close to users for lower latency. Integrates with AWS Shield and AWS WAF; origins include S3, EC2 and load balancers.
cards.official: Amazon CloudFront is a fast content delivery network (CDN) service that securely delivers data, videos, applications, and APIs to customers globally with low latency, high transfer speeds, all within a developer-friendly environment.

cards.eli12: Routes users over AWS global network to healthy endpoints.
cards.definition: Gives your application two static anycast IP addresses and routes users over the AWS global network to the closest healthy endpoint for better availability and performance. Unlike CloudFront it does not cache content and works for TCP/UDP (non-HTTP) traffic.
cards.official: AWS Global Accelerator is a network layer service that you use to create accelerators that direct traffic to optimal endpoints over the AWS global network. This improves the availability and performance of your internet applications that are used by a global audience.

cards.eli12: Privately connect to services without public internet exposure.
cards.definition: Privately connects your VPC to supported AWS services, services in other VPCs and SaaS services through interface VPC endpoints, so traffic never crosses the public internet.
cards.official: AWS PrivateLink simplifies the security of data shared with cloud-based applications by eliminating the exposure of data to the public Internet. AWS PrivateLink provides private connectivity between VPCs, AWS services, and on-premises applications, securely on the Amazon network.

cards.eli12: Central hub connecting many VPCs and networks.
cards.definition: Connects VPCs and on-premises networks through a central hub.
cards.official: AWS Transit Gateway is a service that enables customers to connect their Amazon Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) and their on-premises networks to a single gateway.

cards.eli12: Encrypted connection from an on-prem network to AWS.
cards.definition: IPsec VPN between an on-premises network and AWS.
cards.official: You can optionally connect your VPC to your own corporate data center using an IPsec AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection, making the AWS Cloud an extension of your data center.

cards.eli12: Secure remote access for individual users.
cards.definition: Managed client-based VPN for remote users.
cards.official: For managing remote access, AWS Client VPN connects your users to AWS or on-premises resources using a VPN software client.

cards.eli12: Create/manage APIs that applications call.
cards.definition: Managed service to create, publish, monitor, and secure APIs.
cards.official: Amazon API Gateway is a fully managed service that makes it easy for developers to create, publish, maintain, monitor, and secure APIs at any scale. With a few clicks in the AWS Management Console, you can create an API that acts as a “front door” for applications to access data, business logic, or functionality from your back-end services, such as workloads running on Amazon EC2, code running on AWS Lambda, or any web application.

cards.eli12: Query S3 data with SQL without managing servers.
cards.definition: Serverless, interactive query service to analyze data directly in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. No infrastructure or loading; pay per query based on the amount of data scanned.
cards.official: Amazon Athena is an interactive query service that makes it easy to analyze data in Amazon S3 using standard SQL. Athena is serverless, so there is no infrastructure to manage, and you pay only for the queries that you run.

cards.eli12: Discovers, cleans, and prepares data for analytics.
cards.definition: Serverless data integration service with ETL and Data Catalog capabilities.
cards.official: AWS Glue is a fully managed extract, transform, and load (ETL) service that makes it easy for customers to prepare and load their data for analytics.

cards.eli12: Handles continuous real-time data streams.
cards.definition: Collects, processes, and analyzes real-time streaming data.
cards.official: Amazon Kinesis Data Streams is a massively scalable and durable real-time data streaming service. Kinesis Data Streams can continuously capture gigabytes of data per second from hundreds of thousands of sources such as website clickstreams, database event streams, financial transactions, social media feeds, IT logs, and location-tracking events.

cards.eli12: Turns data into charts and dashboards.
cards.definition: Cloud business intelligence and visualization service.
cards.official: [Amazon] Quick is a fast, cloud-powered business intelligence (BI) service that makes it easy for you to deliver insights to everyone in your organization. QuickSight lets you create and publish interactive dashboards that can be accessed from browsers or mobile devices.

cards.eli12: Routes events from apps/services to targets.
cards.definition: Serverless event bus for event-driven applications.
cards.official: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that makes it easier to build event-driven applications at scale using events generated from your applications, integrated Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) applications, and AWS services.

cards.eli12: Coordinates tasks/services in a workflow.
cards.definition: Serverless workflow orchestration service.
cards.official: AWS Step Functions is a fully managed service that makes it easy to coordinate the components of distributed applications and microservices using visual workflows.

cards.eli12: Send emails at scale from apps.
cards.definition: Cloud email service for sending and receiving email.
cards.official: Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) is a cost-effective, flexible, and scalable email service that enables developers to send mail from within any application. You can configure Amazon SES quickly to support several email use cases, including transactional, marketing, or mass email communications.

cards.eli12: Detailed raw AWS cost and usage reporting.
cards.definition: The most comprehensive, granular AWS billing data: hourly or daily line items for every service, delivered to an S3 bucket for analysis with Athena, QuickSight or Redshift. (Now delivered through AWS Data Exports.)
cards.official: The AWS Cost and Usage Report is a single location for accessing comprehensive information about your AWS costs and usage. The AWS Cost and Usage Report lists AWS usage for each service category used by an account and its IAM users in hourly or daily line items, as well as any tags that you have activated for cost allocation purposes.

cards.eli12: Buy third-party software/services for AWS.
cards.definition: Digital catalog for third-party software and services.
cards.official: AWS Marketplace is a curated digital catalog that customers can use to find, buy, deploy, and manage third-party software, data, and services to build solutions and run their businesses.

cards.eli12: Simplified virtual servers for small apps/sites.
cards.definition: Easiest way to launch virtual private servers: bundles compute, storage, networking and a static IP for a low, predictable monthly price. Best for simple websites, WordPress, blogs and small apps.
cards.official: Amazon Lightsail is designed to be the easiest way to launch and manage a virtual private server with AWS. Lightsail plans include everything you need to jumpstart your project – a VM, SSD-based storage, data transfer, DNS management, and a static IP address – for a low, predictable price.

cards.eli12: AWS-managed infrastructure installed on-premises.
cards.definition: Fully managed AWS racks and servers installed in your own data center, running AWS services with the same APIs and tools, for workloads needing low latency to on-prem systems, local data processing or data residency.
cards.official: AWS Outposts bring native AWS services, infrastructure, and operating models to virtually any data center, co-location space, or on-premises facility. You can use the same APIs, the same tools, the same hardware, and the same functionality across on-premises and the cloud to deliver a truly consistent hybrid experience.

cards.eli12: Stores container images.
cards.definition: Managed container image registry.
cards.official: Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) is a fully managed Docker container registry that makes it easy for developers to store, manage, and deploy Docker container images.

cards.eli12: Runs and manages containers with AWS orchestration.
cards.definition: Fully managed container orchestration service.
cards.official: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) is a highly scalable, high-performance container orchestration service that supports Docker containers and allows you to easily run and scale containerized applications on AWS.

cards.eli12: Runs Kubernetes on AWS.
cards.definition: Managed Kubernetes service.
cards.official: Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) makes it easy to deploy, manage, and scale containerized applications using Kubernetes on AWS. Amazon EKS runs the Kubernetes management infrastructure for you across multiple AWS Availability Zones to eliminate a single point of failure.

cards.eli12: Keeps frequently used data in memory for speed.
cards.definition: Fully managed in-memory caching (Redis OSS, Valkey, Memcached) that gives microsecond latency and reduces load on databases for read-heavy or compute-intensive workloads.
cards.official: Amazon ElastiCache is a web service that makes it easy to deploy, operate, and scale an in-memory cache in the cloud. The service improves the performance of web applications by allowing you to retrieve information from fast, managed, in-memory caches, instead of relying entirely on slower disk-based databases.

cards.eli12: Database for highly connected/relationship data.
cards.definition: Managed graph database service.
cards.official: Amazon Neptune is a fast, reliable, fully managed graph database service that makes it easy to build and run applications that work with highly connected datasets.

cards.eli12: Managed document database for JSON-like data.
cards.definition: Managed document database with MongoDB compatibility.
cards.official: Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) is a fast, scalable, highly available, and fully managed document database service that supports MongoDB workloads.

cards.eli12: Manage AWS from a command line.
cards.definition: Command-line interface for AWS services.
cards.official: AWS Command Line Interface is a unified downloadable and configurable tool for managing AWS services. Control multiple AWS services from the command line and automate them through scripts.

cards.eli12: Compiles source code and runs tests.
cards.definition: Managed continuous integration build service.
cards.official: AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed build service that compiles source code, runs tests, and produces software packages that are ready to deploy. With CodeBuild, you don't need to provision, manage, and scale your own build servers.

cards.eli12: Automates build/test/deploy stages.
cards.definition: Continuous delivery service for software release workflows.
cards.official: AWS CodePipeline is a fully managed continuous delivery service that helps you automate your release pipelines for fast and reliable application and infrastructure updates. CodePipeline automates the build, test, and deploy phases of your release process every time there is a code change, based on the release model you define.

cards.eli12: Traces app requests to find latency/errors.
cards.definition: Distributed tracing service for applications.
cards.official: AWS X-Ray helps developers analyze and debug distributed applications in production or under development, such as those built using a microservices architecture.

cards.eli12: Cloud desktop for a user.
cards.definition: Managed virtual desktop service.
cards.official: Amazon WorkSpaces is a fully managed, secure cloud desktop service. You can use WorkSpaces to provision either Windows or Linux desktops in just a few minutes and quickly scale to provide thousands of desktops to workers across the globe.

cards.eli12: Streams desktop applications to users.
cards.definition: Managed application streaming service.

cards.eli12: Tools and hosting for frontend/mobile apps.
cards.definition: Platform for building and deploying web/mobile applications.
cards.official: AWS Amplify makes it easy to create, configure, and implement scalable mobile applications powered by AWS. Amplify seamlessly provisions and manages your mobile backend and provides a simple framework to easily integrate your backend with your iOS, Android, Web, and React Native frontends.

cards.eli12: Connects internet-connected devices to AWS.
cards.definition: Managed connectivity and messaging for IoT devices.
cards.official: AWS IoT Core is a managed cloud service that lets connected devices easily and securely interact with cloud applications and other devices. AWS IoT Core can support billions of devices and trillions of messages, and can process and route those messages to AWS endpoints and to other devices reliably and securely.

cards.eli12: Finds sentiment/entities/meaning in text.
cards.definition: Natural language processing service for text insights.
cards.official: Amazon Comprehend uses ML and natural language processing (NLP) to help you uncover the insights and relationships in your unstructured data.

cards.eli12: Build conversational voice/text bots.
cards.definition: Conversational AI service for chat and voice interfaces.
cards.official: Amazon Lex is a fully managed artificial intelligence (AI) service to design, build, test, and deploy conversational interfaces into any application using voice and text.

cards.eli12: Turns text into lifelike speech.
cards.definition: Text-to-speech service.
cards.official: Amazon Polly is a service that turns text into lifelike speech. Amazon Polly lets you create applications that talk, enabling you to build entirely new categories of speech-enabled products.

cards.eli12: Pulls text/forms/tables from documents.
cards.definition: ML service extracting text and structured data from documents.
cards.official: Amazon Textract is a service that automatically extracts text and data from scanned documents. Amazon Textract goes beyond simple optical character recognition (OCR) to also identify the contents of fields in forms and information stored in tables.

cards.eli12: Turns audio into written text.
cards.definition: Automatic speech recognition service.
cards.official: Amazon Transcribe is an automatic speech recognition (ASR) service that makes it easy for customers to automatically convert speech to text.

cards.eli12: Automatically translates text.
cards.definition: Neural machine translation service.
cards.official: Amazon Translate is a neural machine translation service that delivers fast, high-quality, and affordable language translation.

cards.eli12: Automatically adds/removes capacity as demand changes.
cards.definition: Automatically adds or removes capacity (e.g., EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group with min, max and desired sizes) based on demand, schedules or predictions, and replaces unhealthy instances. Gives elasticity: performance at peak, lower cost when quiet.
cards.official: AWS Auto Scaling monitors your applications and automatically adjusts capacity to maintain steady, predictable performance at the lowest possible cost.

cards.eli12: Suggests better resource sizes based on usage.
cards.definition: Recommends optimal AWS resource configurations.
cards.official: AWS Compute Optimizer recommends optimal AWS resources for your workloads to reduce costs and improve performance by using machine learning to analyze historical utilization metrics.

cards.eli12: Sets up and governs a multi-account AWS environment.
cards.definition: Helps establish and govern a secure multi-account environment.
cards.official: AWS Control Tower automates the set-up of a baseline environment, or landing zone, that is a secure, well-architected multi-account AWS environment.

cards.eli12: Shows service events that may affect your account/resources.
cards.definition: Shows the general status of AWS services (Service health) and personalized alerts about AWS events and scheduled changes that affect your own resources (Your account health), with remediation guidance.
cards.official: AWS Health provides alerts and remediation guidance when AWS is experiencing events that might affect you.

cards.eli12: View/manage AWS service limits.
cards.definition: Service for viewing and managing AWS quotas.
cards.official: With Service Quotas, you can view and manage your quotas for AWS services from a central location. Quotas, also referred to as limits in AWS services, are the maximum values for the resources, actions, and items in your AWS account.

cards.eli12: Central tools to operate, patch, and manage resources.
cards.definition: Operations hub for managing EC2 and on-premises servers at scale: patch automatically (Patch Manager), connect without SSH or bastion hosts (Session Manager), run commands across a fleet and store configuration data (Parameter Store).
cards.official: AWS Systems Manager gives you visibility and control of your infrastructure on AWS.

cards.eli12: Reviews workloads against AWS architecture best practices.
cards.definition: Tool for reviewing workloads using the Well-Architected Framework.
cards.official: The AWS Well-Architected Tool (AWS WA Tool) helps you review the state of your workloads and compares them to the latest AWS architectural best practices.

cards.eli12: Lift-and-shift servers/apps to AWS.
cards.definition: Primary service for rehosting (lift-and-shift): continuously replicates physical, virtual or cloud servers to AWS and launches them with minimal downtime and no code changes.
cards.official: AWS Transform MGN (AWS MGN) allows you to quickly realize the benefits of migrating applications to the cloud without changes and with minimal downtime.

cards.eli12: Migrates databases with minimal downtime.
cards.definition: AWS Database Migration Service migrates databases to AWS quickly and securely; the source database stays fully operational during migration, minimizing downtime. Supports homogeneous (Oracle → Oracle) and heterogeneous (Oracle → Aurora, with AWS SCT) migrations and continuous replication.
cards.official: AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) helps you migrate databases to AWS easily and securely. The source database remains fully operational during the migration, minimizing downtime to applications that rely on the database.

cards.eli12: One place to track migration progress.
cards.definition: Central location to track migrations to AWS.
cards.official: AWS Migration Hub provides a single location to track the progress of application migrations across multiple AWS and partner solutions.

cards.eli12: Converts database schemas/code between engines.
cards.definition: Schema conversion tool for heterogeneous database migrations.

cards.eli12: Manages certificates used for HTTPS.
cards.definition: Provisions, manages and deploys public and private SSL/TLS certificates for AWS services like Elastic Load Balancing, CloudFront and API Gateway. Public certificates are free and renew automatically.
cards.official: AWS Certificate Manager is a service that lets you easily provision, manage, and deploy Secure Sockets Layer/Transport Layer Security (SSL/TLS) certificates for use with AWS services and your internal connected resources.

cards.eli12: Dedicated hardware security modules for cryptographic keys.
cards.definition: Dedicated, single-tenant hardware security modules in the AWS Cloud. You alone manage the keys — AWS cannot access them. Use when compliance requires dedicated HSMs you control (FIPS 140 validated).
cards.official: The AWS CloudHSM is a cloud-based hardware security module (HSM) that enables you to easily generate and use your own encryption keys on the AWS Cloud. With AWS CloudHSM, you can manage your own encryption keys using dedicated FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated HSMs.

cards.eli12: Adds customer signup/sign-in to apps.
cards.definition: Adds sign-up, sign-in and access control to web and mobile apps for your customers (not employees). Scales to millions of users and supports sign-in with social providers (Google, Facebook, Apple) and enterprise identity providers.
cards.official: Amazon Cognito lets you add user sign-up, sign-in, and access control to your web and mobile apps quickly and easily. With Amazon Cognito, you can scale to millions of users and supports sign-in with social identity providers such as Apple, Facebook, Twitter, or Amazon, with SAML 2.0 identity solutions, or by using your own identity system.

cards.eli12: Helps figure out what happened after suspicious activity.
cards.definition: Analyzes security data to investigate findings and root causes.
cards.official: Amazon Detective makes it easy to analyze, investigate, and quickly identify the root cause of potential security issues or suspicious activities.

cards.eli12: Manages firewall/security policies across accounts.
cards.definition: Central management of firewall policies across AWS Organizations.
cards.official: AWS Firewall Manager is a security management service which allows you to centrally configure and manage firewall rules across your accounts and applications in AWS Organizations.

cards.eli12: Watches for suspicious/malicious activity.
cards.definition: Intelligent threat detection that continuously analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC Flow Logs and DNS logs using machine learning and threat intelligence to find malicious activity (compromised instances, unusual API calls). No agents or software to deploy.
cards.official: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that continuously monitors for malicious activity and anomalous behavior to protect your AWS accounts, workloads, Kubernetes clusters, and data stored in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3). The GuardDuty service monitors for activity such as unusual API calls, unauthorized deployments, and exfiltrated credentials that indicate a possible account reconnaissance or compromise.

cards.eli12: Central sign-in/access across AWS accounts/apps.
cards.definition: Successor to AWS Single Sign-On: gives your workforce one sign-in to access multiple AWS accounts in AWS Organizations and business applications, using its own directory or an external identity provider (e.g., Microsoft Entra ID, Okta).
cards.official: AWS IAM Identity Center (SSO) is a cloud SSO service that makes it easy to centrally manage SSO access to multiple AWS accounts and business applications.

cards.eli12: Creates/controls keys used to encrypt data.
cards.definition: AWS Key Management Service: create and control encryption keys used to encrypt data across AWS services (S3, EBS, RDS and more). Keys are protected by AWS-managed hardware security modules and never leave KMS unencrypted; key use is logged in CloudTrail.
cards.official: AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) makes it easy for you to create and manage cryptographic keys and control their use across a wide range of AWS services and in your applications.

cards.eli12: Finds sensitive data such as PII in S3.
cards.definition: Uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover, classify and protect sensitive data such as personally identifiable information (PII) and financial data stored in Amazon S3.
cards.official: Amazon Macie is a fully managed data security and data privacy service that uses inventory evaluations, machine learning, and pattern matching to discover sensitive data and accessibility in your Amazon S3 environment.

cards.eli12: Stores and rotates secrets securely.
cards.definition: Stores database credentials, API keys and other secrets securely and rotates them automatically on a schedule (e.g., RDS passwords), so apps fetch secrets at runtime instead of hard-coding them.
cards.official: AWS Secrets Manager helps you protect secrets needed to access your applications, services, and IT resources. The service enables you to easily rotate, manage, and retrieve database credentials, API keys, and other secrets throughout their lifecycle.

cards.eli12: Brings security findings together.
cards.definition: Single place to see and prioritize security findings aggregated from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie and partner tools, plus automated checks against security best practices and standards (e.g., CIS, PCI DSS).
cards.official: AWS Security Hub CSPM is a cloud security posture management service that performs automated, continuous security best practice checks against your AWS resources. Security Hub CSPM aggregates your security alerts (i.e. findings) from various AWS services and partner products in a standardized format so that you can more easily take action on them.

cards.eli12: Run containers without managing EC2 servers.
cards.definition: Serverless compute engine for containers on Amazon ECS and EKS: you run containers without provisioning or managing EC2 servers, and pay for the vCPU and memory your containers use.
cards.official: AWS Fargate is a compute engine for Amazon ECS that allows you to run containers without having to manage servers or clusters. With AWS Fargate, you no longer have to provision, configure, and scale clusters of VMs to run containers.

cards.eli12: Centralizes and automates backups.
cards.definition: Managed centralized backup/data protection service.
cards.official: AWS Backup enables you to centralize and automate data protection across AWS services. AWS Backup offers a cost-effective, fully managed, policy-based service that further simplifies data protection at scale.

cards.eli12: Block storage volume commonly attached to EC2.
cards.definition: Persistent block storage volumes for EC2. A volume lives in one Availability Zone and attaches to an instance in that AZ; data persists after the instance stops. Back up with point-in-time snapshots stored in S3. Pay for the size you provision.
cards.official: Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) provides persistent block storage volumes for use with Amazon EC2 instances in the AWS Cloud. Each Amazon EBS volume is automatically replicated within its Availability Zone to protect you from component failure, offering high availability and durability.

cards.eli12: Shared elastic file system for multiple resources.
cards.definition: Serverless, fully managed NFS file system for Linux that many EC2 instances (and containers/Lambda) can mount at the same time, across multiple AZs. Grows and shrinks automatically; pay only for storage used.
cards.official: Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) provides a simple, scalable, elastic file system for Linux-based workloads for use with AWS Cloud services and on-premises resources. It is built to scale on demand to petabytes without disrupting applications, growing and shrinking automatically as you add and remove files.

cards.eli12: Managed file systems such as Windows and Lustre.
cards.definition: Fully managed third-party file systems: FSx for Windows File Server (SMB, Active Directory), FSx for Lustre (high-performance computing/ML), FSx for NetApp ONTAP and FSx for OpenZFS.
cards.official: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a fully managed native Microsoft Windows file system so you can easily move your Windows-based applications that require file storage to AWS. Amazon FSx for Lustre is a fully managed file system that is optimized for compute-intensive workloads, such as high performance computing, machine learning, and media data processing workflows.

cards.eli12: Low-cost storage for rarely accessed long-term data.
cards.definition: Family of low-cost S3 archive storage classes: Glacier Instant Retrieval (milliseconds), Glacier Flexible Retrieval (minutes to hours) and Glacier Deep Archive (hours; cheapest). Trade retrieval speed and retrieval fees for very low storage cost.

cards.eli12: Connects on-prem storage to AWS storage.
cards.definition: Hybrid cloud storage service that gives on-premises applications access to virtually unlimited AWS cloud storage, with local caching. Types: S3 File Gateway, Volume Gateway and Tape Gateway (virtual tape library backups to S3/Glacier).
cards.official: The AWS Storage Gateway is a hybrid storage service that allows your on-premises applications to seamlessly use AWS cloud storage. You can use the service for backup and archiving, disaster recovery, cloud data processing, storage tiering, and migration.

cards.hint: AWS = OF cloud; YOU = IN cloud
cards.eli12: AWS secures cloud infrastructure; you secure/configure your workloads/data.
cards.definition: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud: physical data centers, hardware, networking and the virtualization layer. The customer is responsible for security IN the cloud: their data, IAM, guest OS patching (on EC2), network and firewall configuration, and encryption choices. Shared controls include patch management, configuration management and awareness/training.
cards.official: The AWS Cloud enables a shared responsibility model. While AWS manages security of the cloud, you are responsible for security in the cloud. This means that you retain control of the security you choose to implement to protect your own content, platform, applications, systems, and networks no differently than you would in an on-site data center.

cards.eli12: A geographic area containing multiple Availability Zones.
cards.definition: Separate geographic area that contains multiple (at least 3), isolated Availability Zones. Choose a Region based on compliance and data-residency requirements, proximity to customers (latency), available services and pricing.
cards.official: An AWS Region is a physical location in the world where we have multiple Availability Zones. Availability Zones consist of one or more discrete data centers, each with redundant power, networking, and connectivity, housed in separate facilities.

cards.eli12: Isolated data-center location within a Region.
cards.definition: One or more discrete data centers with redundant power, networking and connectivity within a Region, physically separated from other AZs by a meaningful distance but connected with low-latency links. Deploy across multiple AZs for high availability.
cards.official: A distinct location within a Region that's insulated from failures in other Availability Zones, and provides inexpensive, low-latency network connectivity to other Availability Zones in the same Region.

cards.eli12: Grow and shrink resources as demand changes.
cards.definition: Dynamic acquisition/release of resources to match demand.
cards.official: Stop guessing capacity: ... You can access as much or as little capacity as you need, and scale up and down as required with only a few minutes' notice.

cards.eli12: Increase capacity to handle more work.
cards.definition: Ability to increase/decrease capacity for workload needs.

cards.eli12: Add more resource instances.
cards.definition: Scale by adding/removing resource instances.

cards.eli12: Make one resource more powerful.
cards.definition: Scale by changing capacity of one resource.

cards.eli12: AWS best-practice framework for good cloud architecture.
cards.definition: Best practices across Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, and Sustainability.
cards.official: The AWS Well-Architected Framework ... provides a consistent set of best practices for customers and partners to evaluate architectures, and provides a set of questions you can use to evaluate how well an architecture is aligned to AWS best practices. The AWS Well-Architected Framework is based on six pillars — operational excellence, security, reliability, performance efficiency, cost optimization, and sustainability.

cards.eli12: No long commitment; pay for capacity used.
cards.definition: Pay for compute by the second or hour with no long-term commitment or upfront payment. Highest per-hour price. Best for short-term, spiky or unpredictable workloads that can't be interrupted, and for testing.
cards.official: On-Demand Instances – Pay, by the second, for the instances that you launch.

cards.eli12: Term commitment for discounted eligible usage.
cards.definition: Commit to a specific instance configuration (instance type, Region, OS, tenancy) for a 1- or 3-year term for up to 72% off On-Demand. Payment options: All Upfront (biggest discount), Partial Upfront, No Upfront. Standard RIs give the biggest discount; Convertible RIs can be exchanged for different instance families.
cards.official: Reserved Instances – Reduce your Amazon EC2 costs by making a commitment to a consistent instance configuration, including instance type and Region, for a term of 1 or 3 years.

cards.eli12: Deep discount on spare EC2 capacity that can be interrupted.
cards.definition: Unused EC2 capacity at up to 90% off On-Demand. AWS can reclaim the instance with a 2-minute warning, so use only for fault-tolerant, flexible, stateless workloads (batch jobs, data analysis, CI/CD, image rendering).
cards.official: Spot Instances – Request unused EC2 instances, which can reduce your Amazon EC2 costs significantly.

cards.eli12: Commit to compute usage for lower rates.
cards.definition: Commit to a consistent amount of compute usage ($/hour) for 1 or 3 years. EC2 Instance Savings Plans: up to 72% off, tied to one instance family in one Region (flexible on size, OS, tenancy). Compute Savings Plans: up to 66% off, apply automatically across EC2 (any family, size, Region, OS), Fargate and Lambda. Usage above the commitment is billed On-Demand.
cards.official: Savings Plans is a flexible pricing model offering lower prices compared to On-Demand pricing, in exchange for a specific usage commitment (measured in $/hour) for a one or three-year period. AWS offers three types of Savings Plans – Compute Savings Plans, Amazon EC2 Instance Savings Plans, and Amazon SageMaker AI Savings Plans.

cards.eli12: Estimate AWS costs before deploying.
cards.definition: Free web tool to estimate the cost of AWS services for a planned architecture before you build anything. No AWS account needed; estimates can be exported and shared.

cards.hint: buy hardware → pay as you use
cards.eli12: Cloud reduces big upfront hardware purchases in favor of variable spending.
cards.definition: Cloud economics emphasize variable operating expense over upfront capital expense.
cards.official: Trade fixed expense for variable expense: Instead of having to invest heavily in data centers and servers before you know how you're going to use them, you can pay only when you consume computing resources, and pay only for how much you consume.

cards.eli12: 5G edge infrastructure; current CLF-C02 guide lists Wavelength out of scope.
cards.definition: Edge infrastructure for ultra-low-latency 5G applications; currently out of scope for CLF-C02.
cards.official: AWS Wavelength is an AWS Infrastructure offering optimized for mobile edge computing applications. Wavelength Zones are AWS infrastructure deployments that embed AWS compute and storage services within communications service providers' (CSP) datacenters at the edge of the 5G network, so application traffic from 5G devices can reach application servers running in Wavelength Zones without leaving the telecommunications network.

cards.eli12: Managed big-data processing using Spark/Hadoop.
cards.definition: Managed platform for processing large datasets with open-source analytics frameworks.
cards.official: Amazon EMR is the industry-leading cloud big data platform for processing vast amounts of data using open source tools such as Apache Spark, Apache Hive, Apache HBase, Apache Flink, Apache Hudi, and Presto. Amazon EMR makes it easy to set up, operate, and scale your big data environments by automating time-consuming tasks such as provisioning capacity and tuning clusters.

cards.eli12: Managed search and analytics engine.
cards.definition: Managed OpenSearch for search, log analytics, and observability.
cards.official: Amazon OpenSearch Service (OpenSearch Service) makes it easy to deploy, secure, operate, and scale OpenSearch to search, analyze, and visualize data in real-time.

cards.eli12: Build a customer-service/call center in AWS.
cards.definition: Cloud-based contact center service.
cards.official: [Amazon] Connect Customer is a self-service, omnichannel cloud contact center service that makes it easy for any business to deliver better customer service at lower cost.

cards.eli12: Runs batches of compute jobs at scale.
cards.definition: Managed service for scheduling and running batch computing workloads.
cards.official: AWS Batch enables developers, scientists, and engineers to easily and efficiently run hundreds of thousands of batch computing jobs on AWS. AWS Batch dynamically provisions the optimal quantity and type of compute resources (such as CPU or memory-optimized instances) based on the volume and specific resource requirements of the batch jobs submitted.

cards.eli12: Secure browser access to websites/SaaS.
cards.definition: Managed secure browser service.

cards.eli12: AWS generative AI assistant for work/developer tasks.
cards.definition: Generative AI assistant family for business and developer use cases.
cards.official: Amazon Q is a generative AI-powered assistant for accelerating software development and leveraging your internal data.

cards.eli12: Tools for creating and deploying ML models.
cards.definition: Managed service to build, train, and deploy ML models.
cards.official: With Amazon SageMaker AI, you can build, train, and deploy ML models for any use case with fully managed infrastructure, tools, and workflows. SageMaker AI removes the heavy lifting from each step of the ML process to make it easier to develop high-quality models.

cards.eli12: Tracks software license usage.
cards.definition: Manages software licenses across AWS and hybrid environments.
cards.official: AWS License Manager makes it easier to manage licenses in AWS and on-premises servers from software vendors such as Microsoft, SAP, Oracle, and IBM.

cards.eli12: Collects server info before migration.
cards.definition: Collects on-premises configuration and usage data for migration planning.
cards.official: AWS Application Discovery Service helps enterprise customers plan migration projects by gathering information about their on-premises data centers.

cards.eli12: Estimates costs and builds a migration case.
cards.definition: Assessment service for migration business cases and cost projections.

cards.eli12: Managed directory options including Microsoft AD.
cards.definition: Managed directory services for AWS workloads.
cards.official: AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory, also known as AWS Managed Microsoft AD, enables your directory-aware workloads and AWS resources to use managed Active Directory in the AWS Cloud.

cards.eli12: Shares supported AWS resources between accounts.
cards.definition: Service for sharing supported resources across accounts/Organizations.
cards.official: AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) helps you securely share your resources across AWS accounts, within your organization or organizational units (OUs) in AWS Organizations, and with IAM roles and IAM users for supported resource types.

cards.eli12: Replicates servers so they can recover in AWS.
cards.definition: Service for scalable application recovery to AWS.
cards.official: AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery (Elastic Disaster Recovery) minimizes downtime and data loss with fast, reliable recovery of on-premises and cloud-based applications using affordable storage, minimal compute, and point-in-time recovery.

cards.eli12: Requires another factor besides a password.
cards.definition: Multi-factor authentication requires a second factor (virtual authenticator app, FIDO security key or hardware TOTP token) in addition to a password. AWS strongly recommends MFA on the root user and all IAM users.
cards.official: MFA adds extra security that requires users to provide unique authentication from an AWS supported MFA mechanism ...

cards.eli12: Give only the permissions required.
cards.definition: Grant only the minimum permissions necessary.

cards.eli12: All-powerful account identity; avoid routine use.
cards.definition: Identity created with the AWS account (email + password) that has complete, unrestricted access. Secure it with MFA, don't create access keys for it, and don't use it for everyday tasks. Only root can do a few things, such as close the account, change account settings and change the support plan.
cards.official: When you first create an AWS account, you begin with a default set of credentials with complete access to all AWS resources in your account. Because a root user can perform privileged actions, it's crucial to add MFA for the root user as a second authentication factor in addition to the email address and password as sign-in credentials. Instead of accessing the root user, create an administrative user for everyday tasks.

cards.eli12: Encrypt data while stored.
cards.definition: Encryption protecting stored data.
cards.official: Encrypt: To use a mathematical algorithm to make data unintelligible to unauthorized users. Encryption also gives authorized users a method (such as a key or password) to convert the altered data back to its original state.

cards.eli12: Encrypt data while it travels.
cards.definition: Encryption protecting moving data, commonly with TLS.

cards.eli12: Combine billing across Organization accounts.
cards.definition: AWS Organizations feature that combines all member accounts into one bill paid by the management account. Usage is aggregated for volume pricing tiers, and RI/Savings Plans discounts can be shared. No extra charge.
cards.official: A feature of the AWS Organizations service for consolidating payment for multiple AWS accounts. You create an organization that contains your AWS accounts, and you use the management account of your organization to pay for all member accounts.

cards.eli12: Labels resources so spending can be grouped.
cards.definition: Key-value labels on resources (e.g., Project=Alpha) that, once activated in the Billing console, let you track and group costs by team, project or environment in Cost Explorer and Cost and Usage Reports. Types: AWS-generated and user-defined.
cards.official: A tag is a label that you or AWS assigns to an AWS resource. Each tag consists of a key and a value. You can use tags to organize your resources, and cost allocation tags to track your AWS costs on a detailed level.

cards.eli12: Entire physical EC2 server dedicated to you.
cards.definition: An entire physical EC2 server dedicated to you, with visibility into its sockets and cores. Lets you use existing server-bound software licenses (BYOL, e.g., Windows Server, SQL Server) and meet compliance requirements. Most expensive EC2 option.
cards.official: Dedicated Hosts – Pay for a physical host that is fully dedicated to running your instances, and bring your existing per-socket, per-core, or per-VM software licenses to reduce costs.

cards.eli12: Instances run on single-tenant hardware.
cards.definition: EC2 instances on hardware dedicated to a single customer, but without visibility or control over the physical host (no socket/core info). Use for isolation requirements; use Dedicated Hosts when you need license or host control.
cards.official: Dedicated Instances – Pay, by the hour, for instances that run on single-tenant hardware.

cards.eli12: Reserve EC2 capacity in a specific AZ.
cards.definition: On-Demand Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 capacity in a specific AZ for any duration, so the capacity is there when you need it. You pay the On-Demand rate whether you use it or not; no discount unless combined with Savings Plans or Regional RIs.
cards.official: Capacity Reservations – Reserve capacity for your EC2 instances in a specific Availability Zone.

cards.eli12: Use eligible software licenses you already own.
cards.definition: Bring Your Own License strategy for existing eligible licenses.

cards.eli12: Match resource size to actual workload need.
cards.definition: Adjust resource types/sizes to improve cost and performance.

cards.eli12: Libraries that let apps call AWS services.
cards.definition: Software development kits for accessing AWS from programming languages.

cards.eli12: A defined way programs request actions/data.
cards.definition: Interface enabling software components to communicate programmatically.

cards.eli12: Community knowledge for AWS technical questions.
cards.definition: AWS-managed community knowledge service.
cards.official: AWS re:Post (re:Post), a new, community-driven, questions-and-answers service ...

cards.eli12: Strategies, guides, and patterns for cloud projects.
cards.definition: AWS technical guidance with strategies, guides, and patterns.

cards.eli12: Community of companies providing AWS solutions/services.
cards.definition: Global partner program for technology and consulting organizations.

cards.eli12: AWS experts help plan/execute cloud initiatives.
cards.definition: AWS consulting experts helping customers achieve cloud outcomes.

cards.eli12: Entry support resources, not full technical engineering support.
cards.definition: Free for every AWS account: 24/7 customer service for billing and account questions, documentation, whitepapers, AWS re:Post, the AWS Health Dashboard and core Trusted Advisor checks. No technical support cases.
cards.official: Basic Support offers assistance for account and billing questions and service quota increases.

cards.eli12: Current support option for production workloads needing 24/7 technical help.
cards.definition: New AWS plan (launched late 2025, from $29/month) for production workloads: 24/7 AI-powered assistance with direct access to AWS experts; experts respond within 30 minutes for critical cases. Replaces Developer, Business and Enterprise On-Ramp Support.

cards.eli12: Current support offering for complex operational environments.
cards.definition: Highest AWS support tier (from $50,000/month): a dedicated core team (TAM, Domain Engineer, Senior Billing and Account Specialist), on-demand experts for migration, incidents and security, around-the-clock monitoring, and 5-minute response for critical incidents.

cards.eli12: Cloud lets a business deploy quickly, reach users globally, and change capacity without buying hardware first.
cards.definition: AWS's six advantages of cloud computing: trade fixed (capital) expense for variable expense; benefit from massive economies of scale; stop guessing capacity; increase speed and agility; stop spending money running and maintaining data centers; go global in minutes.
cards.official: Six advantages of cloud computing: Trade fixed expense for variable expense; Benefit from massive economies of scale; Stop guessing capacity; Increase speed and agility; Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers; Go global in minutes.

cards.eli12: Cloud resources can be created and changed quickly.
cards.definition: Ability to rapidly provision, experiment, and respond to changing business needs.
cards.official: In a cloud computing environment, new IT resources are only a click away, which means that you reduce the time to make those resources available to your developers from weeks to just minutes. This results in a dramatic increase in agility for the organization, since the cost and time it takes to experiment and develop is significantly lower.

cards.eli12: Moving to cloud can reduce infrastructure burden and improve agility, reach, resilience, and economics.
cards.definition: Business and technical benefits gained by migrating workloads to AWS.

cards.hint: PLAN the move, not just MOVE
cards.eli12: Organizations use structured strategies and AWS resources to plan cloud adoption and migration.
cards.definition: Migration strategies — the 7 Rs: Rehost (lift and shift), Replatform (lift, tinker and shift), Refactor/re-architect (rebuild cloud-native), Repurchase (move to SaaS), Relocate (e.g., VMware Cloud on AWS), Retain (keep on-premises for now) and Retire (turn off).

cards.eli12: Keep source and destination data synchronized to reduce migration disruption.
cards.definition: Replication can support database migration by copying and synchronizing data between environments.

cards.hint: PHYSICAL box moves LOTS of data
cards.eli12: AWS ships a device so huge datasets can be moved when network transfer is impractical.
cards.definition: Rugged physical device AWS ships to you for moving terabytes to petabytes of data into or out of AWS when network transfer would be too slow or costly. Snowball Edge devices also provide local compute and storage at disconnected edge sites.
cards.official: Snowball Edge is a device with on-board storage and compute power for select AWS capabilities. Snowball Edge can process data locally, run edge-computing workloads, and transfer data to or from the AWS Cloud. (AWS notes Snowball Edge is no longer available to new customers.)

cards.eli12: Buying data-center equipment creates fixed/upfront costs; cloud lets spending follow usage.
cards.definition: Cloud economics shifts many infrastructure costs from fixed capital expense toward variable usage-based expense.
cards.official: Trade fixed expense for variable expense: Instead of having to invest heavily in data centers and servers before you know how you're going to use them, you can pay only when you consume computing resources, and pay only for how much you consume.

cards.hint: Servers cost MORE than the server
cards.eli12: On-prem costs include hardware plus buildings, power, cooling, maintenance, staffing, and capacity planning.
cards.definition: Total on-premises cost includes infrastructure acquisition and ongoing facilities/operations expenses.
cards.official: Stop spending money running and maintaining data centers: Focus on projects that differentiate your business, not the infrastructure. Cloud computing lets you focus on your own customers, rather than on the heavy lifting of racking, stacking, and powering servers.

cards.eli12: Automation makes repeated cloud tasks faster and more consistent.
cards.definition: Automation improves consistency, repeatability, speed, and operational efficiency.

cards.eli12: AWS provides compliance programs/resources, but customers remain responsible for their own requirements.
cards.definition: AWS compliance programs and resources help customers meet regulatory and industry requirements.

cards.term: Shared Responsibility – EC2 vs RDS vs Lambda
cards.eli12: Your responsibilities change depending on how managed the service is.
cards.definition: The more managed the service, the less you manage. EC2 (IaaS): you patch the guest OS and applications and configure security groups.
