cards.hint: strong IDENTITY, TRACEABILITY, security at ALL LAYERS, protect data
cards.eli12: Protecting data, systems and accounts.
cards.definition: Protect information, systems and assets. Principles: strong identity foundation (least privilege, no long-term credentials), enable traceability, apply security at all layers, automate security, protect data in transit and at rest, keep people away from data, prepare for security events. Services: IAM, STS, MFA, Organizations, Config, CloudTrail, CloudWatch, VPC, Shield, WAF, Inspector, KMS.

cards.hint: RECOVER from failure, scale HORIZONTALLY, stop guessing capacity
cards.eli12: Keep working, and bounce back fast when something breaks.
cards.definition: Recover from infrastructure or service disruptions, acquire resources to meet demand, and mitigate issues like misconfigurations. Principles: test recovery procedures, recover automatically, scale horizontally, stop guessing capacity, manage change with automation. Services: Service Quotas, Trusted Advisor, Auto Scaling, CloudWatch, Backup, S3, Route 53.

cards.hint: use resources EFFICIENTLY: go global, serverless, experiment
cards.eli12: Use the right tool for the job and keep it efficient.
cards.definition: Use computing resources efficiently as demand and technology change. Principles: democratize advanced technologies (use them as services), go global in minutes, use serverless, experiment more often, mechanical sympathy (know your services). Services: Auto Scaling, Lambda, EBS, S3, RDS, ElastiCache, CloudFront, CloudWatch.

cards.hint: lowest PRICE: pay for use, measure, TAG and attribute spend
cards.eli12: Get the most value for the least money.
cards.definition: Deliver business value at the lowest price point. Principles: adopt a consumption model (pay only for use), measure overall efficiency, stop spending on data centers, analyze and attribute spending (use tags), use managed services. Services: Budgets, Cost and Usage Report, Cost Explorer, Spot and Reserved Instances, S3 Glacier, Auto Scaling, Lambda, Trusted Advisor.

cards.hint: minimize ENVIRONMENTAL impact: right-size, use efficient hardware
cards.eli12: Using the cloud in a way that's kinder to the planet.
cards.definition: Minimize the environmental impact of cloud workloads. Principles: understand your impact, set sustainability goals, maximize utilization (right-size, avoid idle), adopt more efficient hardware and software, use managed services, reduce downstream impact. Services: Auto Scaling, Lambda, Fargate, Graviton, Spot, EFS-IA, S3 Glacier, S3 lifecycle and Intelligent-Tiering.

cards.eli12: Shows how much pollution your AWS use creates.
cards.definition: Billing console tool to track, measure, review and forecast the carbon emissions from your AWS usage, to support your sustainability goals.

cards.hint: BUSINESS = cloud investments drive BUSINESS OUTCOMES
cards.eli12: Making sure cloud spending helps the business win.
cards.definition: CAF business-capability perspective that ensures cloud investments accelerate digital transformation and business outcomes.

cards.hint: PEOPLE = culture, leadership, workforce, org structure
cards.eli12: Getting people and culture ready for the cloud.
cards.definition: CAF business-capability perspective that bridges technology and business, evolving culture, organizational structure, leadership and workforce toward continuous learning and change.

cards.eli12: Steering the cloud program and keeping risks low.
cards.definition: CAF business-capability perspective that orchestrates cloud initiatives to maximize organizational benefits and minimize transformation risks.

cards.hint: PLATFORM = build a scalable hybrid cloud platform, modernize
cards.eli12: Building the technical foundation in the cloud.
cards.definition: CAF technical-capability perspective for building an enterprise-grade, scalable hybrid cloud platform, modernizing existing workloads and implementing cloud-native solutions.

cards.eli12: Keeping data and workloads safe during the move.
cards.definition: CAF technical-capability perspective focused on achieving the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data and cloud workloads.

cards.hint: OPERATIONS = deliver cloud services at the level the business needs
cards.eli12: Running cloud services well, day to day.
cards.definition: CAF technical-capability perspective that ensures cloud services are delivered at a level that meets business needs.

cards.eli12: Ready-made recipes for common AWS setups.
cards.definition: Collection of vetted, ready-to-deploy technology solutions for common use cases (e.g., live streaming on AWS). Formerly AWS Quick Starts.

cards.hint: digital, classroom & private TRAINING · AWS Academy for universities
cards.eli12: Ways to learn AWS officially.
cards.definition: AWS digital (online) and classroom training (in person or virtual), private training for organizations, programs for government and enterprises, and AWS Academy to help universities teach AWS.

cards.term: AWS Competency Program & APN Partner Types
cards.hint: Technology, Consulting, Training partners · COMPETENCY = proven expertise
cards.eli12: Different kinds of AWS partners and their badges.
cards.definition: APN partner types: Technology partners (hardware, connectivity, software), Consulting partners (firms that help you build on AWS) and Training partners. The AWS Competency Program recognizes partners with proven technical skill and customer success in specialized areas; the Navigate Program helps partners grow.
confuse: AWS Partners: ISVs vs System Integrators

cards.hint: 65 questions · 90 minutes · 700/1000 to pass · no penalty for guessing
cards.eli12: How the test works.
cards.definition: 65 questions in 90 minutes; multiple choice (one correct) and multiple response (two or more correct, and the number is stated). Unanswered questions count as wrong, so always guess. You can flag questions to review. Pass with 700 out of 1000; you see pass/fail right away; retake after 14 days. Eliminate wrong answers and don't overthink — overly complicated answers are usually wrong.
